root_cause: On-chain authorization flaw: second Ed25519 signature verification routed to the first instruction, so the attacker's own signature was accepted a second time; AddCollateralAdmin then made the attacker admin of user collateral accounts, enabling WithdrawCollateralAsset.
fleet: Rain card / collateral-authorization stack shared across card partners (Avici, and per Rain: KAST, Offramp, Rhythmic, ether.fi cards) on Solana/Tron/Stellar/Monad. SlowMist framed it as an outdated shared Rain card contract 'used by a few other programs.'
note: Explicitly not an upgrade-key compromise (upgrade authority unused since 2025-03). Custodial card collateral => real user money.

root_cause: Low-liquidity token MAMO posted as collateral; spot price inflated, then borrowed cbBTC/USDC from mCBTC/mUSDC markets against the inflated valuation.
fleet: Compound/Moonwell-fork lending markets that list low-liquidity tokens as collateral with a manipulable price source.
note: ALREADY COVERED: moonwell-lending / moonwell-vaults in delivered ledger. Validation, not a new candidate.

root_cause: Flaw in _transfer + isSell logic burned tokens incorrectly on sells, letting buy/sell loops drain the FH/USDT PancakeSwap V2 pool.
fleet: Fee/burn-on-transfer tokens whose _transfer mutates balances against a paired AMM reserve (deflationary/reflection tokens). Token-specific, weak fleet.

root_cause: swap_exact_amount_in/out do not require token_in != token_out; a USDC->USDC swap corrupts weighted-pool reserve math. Attacker flash-loaned from a Blend pool and looped ~36x on the BLND-USDC pool (Blend's backstop).
fleet: Comet v1 is a public Balancer-fork template (CometDEX/comet-contracts-v1) reused across Stellar DeFi (Blend backstop, Smol auto-Comet liquidity, other Comet pools). Generalizes to Lens-E distinctness in any weighted-pool AMM on newer VMs (Soroban/Sui/Aptos/Solana).
note: Verified from public source: top-level swap fns only require_auth(); distinctness check absent at that layer. Un-hit relatives = other live Comet pools.

root_cause: Storage-layout mismatch in delegate-call adapters plus an unprotected initialize let the attacker take over the Managed Delegate Proxy via DELEGATECALL, register a malicious adapter, move NFTs from ~52 wallets without approval, and melt them to redeem backing ENJ.
fleet: Legacy delegatecall-adapter proxy systems (old NFT/token platforms) that still hold backing and expose an unprotected initializer or adapter registration.
note: 'Legacy' platform still holding ENJ backing => the forgotten-code-holding-value pattern.

root_cause: Attacker acquired majority voting power (100% of several USDC vaults, ~91% ETH Meta Vault), passed proposals to disable the timelock and drain ~2,843 ETH + 1.68M USDC.
fleet: Vault protocols where deposit shares confer votes and a majority can disable/bypass the timelock and move funds.
note: ALREADY PREDICTED: termfinance-vaults in delivered ledger, termfinance-lend in current urgency list. Strong validation of the prior run's GOV-CHEAP-CONTROL family.

method: Flash-loan spot-price manipulation of LP-share mint/burn
root_cause: mint()/burn() value the Uniswap V3 position via getUnderlyingBalances()->pool.slot0() (instantaneous tick) with no TWAP/deviation guard; the TWAP _checkSlippage(observe()) is reachable only from rebalance(). Attacker flash-loaned 1,800 WETH (Morpho Blue), skewed slot0, minted shares at the distorted valuation, restored price, burned for a richer mix.
fleet: All Arrakis V1 / G-UNI vaults share the mint/burn-off-slot0 code (guard on sibling rebalance() only). 105 vaults enumerated from factory 0xea1aff9d..., 4 impls all same ArrakisVaultV1/GUniPool family. Un-hit siblings hold the money.
note: NEW (not in ledger/urgency list). VERIFIED on-chain. Economic caveat: V1 fleet holds ~$1.2M on mainnet, mostly stablecoin pairs (near-zero skew profit); largest volatile un-hit sibling ETH2x-FLI/WETH ~$198k.

method: Fake-burn mint on source chain, forged validator signatures
root_cause: Chia-side Chialisp puzzle let the attacker mint worthless CAT tokens, present them as burned wUSDC, obtain validator signatures, and drain USDC from Base/Ethereum bridge contracts.
fleet: Small cross-chain messaging bridges that mint/release on a source-chain 'burn' whose identity is established by a permissionless source-chain construct.
note: Niche source chain (Chia). Pattern maps to existing bridge family.

root_cause: Shared Cosmos EVM precompile-layer vulnerability drained ~2.985B TAC from a single account (drain not mint; supply unchanged). Flaw not in TAC-specific code; chain halted at block 24,671,475.
fleet: github.com/cosmos/evm chains with the vulnerable static precompile set.
note: ALREADY COVERED: Cosmos EVM precompile cluster is Tier-2 in the current urgency list (Berachain, Canto, Cronos, ... one row per chain). TAC confirms the cluster is being actively exploited.

method: approveAndCall arbitrary-call -> LayerZero delegate hijack -> unbacked mint
root_cause: OFTSand inherits ERC20BasicApproveExtension: approveAndCall/paidCall perform target.call(data) from the token contract's own context, guarded only by doFirstParamEqualsAddress(data, msg.sender). Because OFTSand is a LayerZero OApp and EndpointV2.setDelegate keys the delegate by msg.sender, an attacker calls approveAndCall(endpoint, 0, setDelegate(attacker)) -> the SAND OApp sets the attacker as its delegate -> attacker configures a malicious DVN/receive-library -> delivers a forged inbound OFT message -> mints unbacked SAND on Base/BNB -> bridges back to unlock ~14.75M real SAND from the Ethereum adapter.
fleet: Any LayerZero OApp/OFT that also exposes an unprivileged arbitrary-target call (approveAndCall/paidCall/transferAndCall/multicall/execute). The arbitrary call reaches endpoint.setDelegate(attacker) regardless of the current delegate. Value at risk = backing locked in that token's OFT adapter(s).
note: NEW class. Mechanism VERIFIED on-chain against SAND Base source (0xac531Eb2...). SAND itself now contained (all peers zeroed, delegate=multisig). The CLASS is the forward lead; the OG SAND on Eth/Polygon have approveAndCall but are NOT OApps, so not hijackable.

method: Forged CCTP message credited without burn-binding
root_cause: On 2026-07-26 the attacker called Circle MessageTransmitterV2.sendMessage on Polygon to forge a CCTP-style message claiming a 1M USDC transfer with no actual burn, and obtained a valid attestation. On 2026-08-19, receiveCctpMessage on the Base Router credited the message body as a real deposit (verified the attestation envelope but not that the source was a real depositForBurn), then the attacker flash-loaned to match and withdrew.
fleet: CCTP integrators that credit off a received message body (generic sendMessage/receiveMessage) instead of binding the credit to a verified DepositForBurn/mint. allbridge-classic already flagged in the current urgency list; the CCTP-router credit pattern is broader.
note: Lens B forgery: envelope-valid != true. Pre-registered message weeks ahead (time is free).
